//: The machine-checkable half of docs/limitations.md's '## Known divergences' section (chtypes#185). The prose is authored there; this file carries only what scripts/check-divergences.py can drive against loaded artifacts. Every '###' heading under that section must have exactly one entry here (by 'heading', matched verbatim, prefix stripped) and every entry here must match a heading — scripts/check-divergences.py's coverage check refuses either side existing alone. Each check's 'settings' are a compile-time profile (a type gate binds at compile, docs/guides/settings.md 'The one exception'); 'err_code' and 'err_msg' are asserted only where docs/limitations.md itself states them — a code without a quoted message means the page named the code alone. 'stored' asserts THIS LIBRARY's current answer for a row's stored text (BatchResult.rows[i].values[column].text) — it is expected to start FAILING the day a relink makes the library match the server, which is the retirement signal for this entry, not a regression.

entries.heading: A later row's Dynamic value in a multi-row text body, typed without the earlier rows

checks.note: the divergence itself: row 2 ('[]') has no type of its own; a real server reuses row 1's Int64 variant and stores 0, this library types row 2 alone and stores String '[]' (server half measured by the artifact producer, not here)
the same shape with a nested-array variant: a real server stores an empty Array(Array(Int64)) ([]), this library stores the String "[]"
the JSON-column form of the same divergence: a real server stores {"a":[[]]} (row 1's Array(Array(Int64)) path reused), this library stores {"a":[null]} as given
contrast: the same values in a CSV body do not diverge — both sides store the String "[]" for row 2
